# LLM usage guide for @photon-ai/unicode-shield

This file is for language models / AI agents that use this package to sanitize
incoming text before processing it. The package has zero runtime dependencies
and works in Node.js, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, and browsers.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. What this package does
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Unicode Shield strips or normalizes dangerous Unicode characters from text.
These characters are invisible to humans but parsed by LLMs, tokenizers, and
downstream systems. They enable hidden text injection, bidi spoofing, homoglyph
phishing, Zalgo obfuscation, and encoding bypass attacks.

iMessage delivers every Unicode character intact -- nothing is stripped in
transport. This package catches all of them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Installation
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

npm install @photon-ai/unicode-shield
# or
bun add @photon-ai/unicode-shield

Zero runtime dependencies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Exports
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The package exports three functions and several types:

Functions:
  - normalize(text, options?)   → string
  - analyze(text, options?)     → AnalyzeResult
  - createShield(options?)      → Shield

Types:
  - ShieldOptions
  - BidiMode
  - FindingType
  - Finding
  - AnalyzeResult
  - Shield

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. normalize(text, options?)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The main function. Strips all problematic characters and returns clean text.
Zero config -- handles everything by default.

  import { normalize } from "@photon-ai/unicode-shield";

  const clean = normalize(userInput);

Examples:
  normalize("Hello\u200BWorld")          → "HelloWorld"
  normalize("Click: \u202Emoc.xyz")      → "Click: moc.xyz"
  normalize("Hello\u00A0World")          → "Hello World"
  normalize("p\u0430ypal")              → "paypal"
  normalize("\uFF28\uFF21\uFF23\uFF2B")  → "HACK"

Override defaults with options:
  normalize(text, { confusables: false })
  normalize(text, { bidi: "escape" })
  normalize(text, { diacritics: 1 })
  normalize(text, { collapseWhitespace: true, trim: true })

When to use: you just need clean text. Most common use case.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. analyze(text, options?)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Same normalization as normalize(), but also returns a report of every character
that was acted on.

  import { analyze } from "@photon-ai/unicode-shield";

  const result = analyze(userInput);
  // result.text     → cleaned string
  // result.dirty    → boolean (true if any threats found)
  // result.findings → array of Finding objects

Each Finding has:
  - type:      FindingType (e.g. "invisible", "bidi", "confusable")
  - codepoint: number (the Unicode codepoint)
  - index:     number (position in the original string)
  - name:      string (human-readable name like "ZERO_WIDTH_SPACE")
  - action:    "stripped" | "escaped" | "normalized"

When to use: you need visibility into what was found -- for logging, alerting,
auditing, or deciding whether to flag a message.

Example:
  const result = analyze(message.text ?? "");
  if (result.dirty) {
    console.log(`Found ${result.findings.length} threats`);
  }
  const clean = result.text;

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. createShield(options?)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Creates a pre-configured instance for repeated use. Returns an object with
normalize() and analyze() methods bound to those options.

  import { createShield } from "@photon-ai/unicode-shield";

  const shield = createShield({
    diacritics: 0,
    collapseWhitespace: true,
    trim: true,
  });

  shield.normalize(text);
  shield.analyze(text);

When to use: you want to reuse the same options across your app without passing
them to every call.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Options (ShieldOptions)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All options are optional. Defaults handle the full attack surface.

  invisibles          boolean        default: true
    Strip zero-width chars, BOM, fillers, invisible operators.

  bidi                "strip" | "escape" | "ignore"    default: "strip"
    "strip"  → remove bidi control characters entirely
    "escape" → replace with [U+XXXX] placeholders
    "ignore" → pass through unchanged

  controls            boolean        default: true
    Strip C0 (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F) and C1 (U+0080-U+009F) control characters.
    Preserves tab (\t), newline (\n), carriage return (\r).

  tags                boolean        default: true
    Strip tag characters (U+E0000-U+E007F). These encode hidden ASCII.

  variationSelectors  boolean        default: true
    Strip variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F, U+E0100-E01EF). 256 total.

  normalizeWhitespace boolean        default: true
    Normalize exotic whitespace (NBSP, Ogham, ideographic, thin/hair spaces)
    to regular ASCII space.

  separators          boolean        default: true
    Strip line separator (U+2028) and paragraph separator (U+2029).

  formatting          boolean        default: true
    Strip interlinear annotations, deprecated formatting, object replacement,
    replacement character, non-characters.

  diacritics          number | false default: 3
    Max combining marks per base character.
    3 = normal accented text preserved, Zalgo stripped.
    0 = strip all combining marks.
    false = disable entirely.

  nfkc                boolean        default: true
    NFKC normalize fullwidth ASCII, math bold/italic, enclosed/circled,
    superscript/subscript to their ASCII equivalents.

  confusables         boolean        default: true
    Normalize Cyrillic/Greek/Armenian/Cherokee homoglyphs to Latin.
    Disable for multilingual apps where users write in those scripts.

  collapseWhitespace  boolean        default: false
    Collapse consecutive spaces/tabs to single space, newlines to one.

  trim                boolean        default: false
    Trim leading and trailing whitespace.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. Types
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  type BidiMode = "strip" | "escape" | "ignore";

  type FindingType =
    | "invisible" | "bidi" | "control" | "tag" | "variation-selector"
    | "special-space" | "separator" | "formatting" | "non-character"
    | "diacritics" | "confusable" | "nfkc";

  interface Finding {
    type: FindingType;
    codepoint: number;
    index: number;
    name: string;
    action: "stripped" | "escaped" | "normalized";
  }

  interface AnalyzeResult {
    text: string;
    dirty: boolean;
    findings: Finding[];
  }

  interface Shield {
    normalize(text: string): string;
    analyze(text: string): AnalyzeResult;
  }

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. Pipeline order
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The normalization pipeline runs in this order:

  1. NFKC normalization (collapses fullwidth/math/enclosed to ASCII)
  2. Character stripping (invisibles, controls, tags, selectors, whitespace,
     separators, formatting)
  3. Bidi processing (strip, escape, or ignore)
  4. Diacritics limiting (Zalgo defense)
  5. Confusable normalization (homoglyph → Latin)
  6. Whitespace collapse (if enabled)
  7. Trim (if enabled)

NFKC runs first so collapsed forms get caught by subsequent steps.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. Usage with Photon iMessage SDKs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

With @photon-ai/advanced-imessage-kit:

  import { SDK } from "@photon-ai/advanced-imessage-kit";
  import { normalize, analyze } from "@photon-ai/unicode-shield";

  const sdk = SDK({ serverUrl: "https://abc123.imsgd.photon.codes" });
  await sdk.connect();

  sdk.on("new-message", async (message) => {
    const result = analyze(message.text ?? "");
    if (result.dirty) {
      console.log(`[SHIELD] ${result.findings.length} threats stripped`);
    }
    const reply = await yourAgent.process(result.text);
    await sdk.messages.sendMessage({
      chatGuid: message.chats?.[0]?.guid ?? `iMessage;-;${message.handle?.address}`,
      message: reply,
    });
  });

With @photon-ai/imessage-kit:

  import { IMessageSDK } from "@photon-ai/imessage-kit";
  import { normalize } from "@photon-ai/unicode-shield";

  const sdk = new IMessageSDK();

  await sdk.startWatching({
    onDirectMessage: async (msg) => {
      const clean = normalize(msg.text ?? "");
      const reply = await yourAgent.process(clean);
      await sdk.send(msg.sender, reply);
    },
    onGroupMessage: async (msg) => {
      const clean = normalize(msg.text ?? "");
      const reply = await yourAgent.process(clean);
      await sdk.send(msg.chatId, reply);
    },
  });

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11. Coverage
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

400+ codepoints across 16 categories. All 51 iMessage attack vectors handled.

Categories:
  - Zero-width and invisible characters (ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, BOM, fillers, etc.)
  - Bidi attack characters (RTL/LTR overrides, embeddings, isolates)
  - Control characters (C0, C1)
  - Tag characters (U+E0000-E007F, 128 chars encoding hidden ASCII)
  - Variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F, U+E0100-E01EF, 256 total)
  - Special whitespace (NBSP, Ogham, ideographic, thin/hair, etc.)
  - Separators (line/paragraph)
  - Annotation and formatting (interlinear, deprecated, non-characters)
  - Musical formatting (U+1D173-1D17A)
  - Shorthand controls (U+1BCA0-1BCA3)
  - Stacked diacritics / Zalgo (all combining mark ranges)
  - Confusable homoglyphs (Cyrillic, Greek, Armenian, Cherokee → Latin)
  - NFKC targets (fullwidth, math alphanumeric, enclosed, super/subscript)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12. Safety notes for LLMs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Always normalize user input BEFORE passing it to your LLM or agent pipeline.
- The normalize() function is pure and side-effect free. Safe to call on every
  message.
- If you need to preserve the original text for logging, use analyze() which
  returns both the cleaned text and the original findings.
- For multilingual apps, disable confusables (confusables: false) to avoid
  normalizing legitimate Cyrillic/Greek text.
- The package does NOT handle non-Unicode attacks (prompt injection via natural
  language, base64 payloads, delimiter injection, etc.). Those require
  prompt-level defenses.
